methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort study from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute of 72 CSCC patients with anti-PD-1 failure selected from 238 treated. Statistical methods include Kaplan-Meier OS/EFS with log-transformation CIs, cumulative incidence with competing-risk sub-distribution hazards, univariate then multivariate Cox regression (variables with P<0.05 advanced), Mann-Whitney U for TMB comparison, and Fisher exact for gene enrichment. The operational definitions (primary vs secondary resistance at 6 months, EFS1 vs EFS2) are explicit. Limitations acknowledged include single-center design, small genomic subset (n=20), unvalidated 6-month cutoff for resistance classification, and heterogeneous subsequent treatments precluding direct comparison. No power calculation; no external validation cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective case series/cohort (Oxford LoE 4). Clinical relevance is strong: the manuscript addresses a pressing gap in managing CSCC after anti-PD-1 failure, where clinical trial data are sparse. Findings include actionable response rates for cetuximab-based salvage therapy, the prognostic association of prior chemotherapy with worse OS (HR 2.87), and a 41% response rate for anti-PD-1 rechallenge in a subset. These directly inform real-world decision-making and trial design, as noted in the discussion regarding I-TACKLE and Alliance A091802.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE applies. The manuscript reports study setting (DF/HCC, April 2016-January 2025), eligibility, inclusion/exclusion (72/238 with progression, excluded those without sufficient follow-up), variable definitions (immunosuppression, primary/secondary resistance, EFS1/EFS2, progression patterns), sequencing criteria (>=20% tumor content, 80-640x depth, 50x QC, 19 genes reported, KEYNOTE-158 TMB threshold of 10/Mb), IRB approval (protocol #22-088), and appropriate Kaplan-Meier and competing-risk analyses. Table 1 provides comprehensive baseline characteristics. Data availability and code are not explicitly described. Reporting is overall thorough with moderate STROBE adherence.

novelty_literature.justification: The study adds new real-world evidence to an understudied question (management after anti-PD-1 failure in CSCC) and provides the first cohort-level association of lower TMB with primary resistance in this setting. Prior work (Marin-Acevedo et al., Mo et al., I-TACKLE trial, Alliance A091802) has explored cetuximab and rechallenge strategies; this study provides supporting evidence and the TMB finding is incremental but meaningful. Not a paradigm-shifting contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear abstract, focused research question, and coherent progression from cohort description to genomic analysis to survival outcomes to subsequent treatments. Figures 1-4 include Sankey, cumulative incidence, Kaplan-Meier, swimmer, and pie chart displays covering the spectrum of clinical course. Table 1 is clean. The writing is precise and acknowledges limitations appropriately. Minor issues include occasional dense paragraphs in the discussion and heavy use of acronyms (anti-PD-1, CSCC, EFS1, EFS2, BOR).

key_strengths: Real-world single-institution cohort of 72 CSCC patients with anti-PD-1 failure, addressing an understudied clinical problem
Rigorous competing-risk analysis for CSCC-specific death with explicit 1, 3, and 5-year cumulative incidence estimates
Novel association between lower tumor mutational burden and primary (vs secondary) resistance in CSCC (P=0.03)
Clinically actionable finding that prior systemic chemotherapy is associated with poorer OS (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.03-7.98)
Comprehensive characterization of salvage treatment landscape (cetuximab, local therapy, rechallenge) with response rates
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability; no external validation cohort
Small genomic subset (n=20/72) limits the TMB and mutation enrichment analyses
Heterogeneous subsequent treatments (cetuximab, local, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, trials) preclude direct comparative efficacy assessment
No multiplicity correction for the multiple Cox models tested in univariate screening
6-month cutoff for primary/secondary resistance is pragmatic but not formally validated
Data availability and code not described
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent, clinically informative single-center retrospective cohort study that addresses a real gap in CSCC management post-anti-PD-1 failure; appropriate for a Tier 3 oncology journal with minor revisions.
